page: Amazon Web Services i8g.8xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom 64-bit ARM architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores using the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB L1D cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 7500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier memory performance, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth at 406.47 GB/sec and write memory bandwidth at 183.77 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Passmark memory scores and database operations also place in the top 10%, while multi-core Geekbench scores reach top-tier levels. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations demonstrate strong performance in the top 25%. However, single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores remain in the average tier.

While the server excels in memory-intensive and database operations, it exhibits limitations in heavy compute tasks such as large-scale language model inference. Prompt processing for a 70B parameter LLM registers in the bottom 25% at 5.91 tokens per second. Consequently, this instance is best suited for high-throughput database systems, caching layers like Redis, and memory-bound data processing, rather than large-scale AI inference workloads.
